name: TextBox 3
text:
In Week 3 your board read a button and drove an LED. This week it measures the real world and acts on it.
Learning outcomes
Sensors: explain what a sensor is and classify its output signal
Signals: tell digital, analog, PWM and protocol devices apart
Reading: get temperature and humidity from a DHT22 into the ESP32
Actuators: drive a servo, and know when a driver or relay is needed
Automation: build rule-based control from one and many conditions

Why Task 1 installs two libraries
The DHT22 encodes 40 bits as pulse widths on a single wire, with timing measured in microseconds.
DHT sensor library decodes that frame; Adafruit Unified Sensor is the shared base class it depends on. Without both, the sketch will not compile.

name: TextBox 7
text:
Two practical rules
Read no faster than once every 2 s — otherwise you get a stale value or NaN. Every sketch this week calls delay(2000).
A bare DHT22 needs a 4.7–10 kΩ pull-up on DATA; breakout modules and the Wokwi part already include it.

name: TextBox 3
text:
Five questions
Is the device digital, analog, PWM or on a bus?
Does it use I²C, SPI, UART or its own protocol?
Is the signal pin 3.3 V or 5 V?
Does it need a pull-up or pull-down resistor?
Do I have enough pins, timers and ADC channels?

name: TextBox 5
text:
Logic level
The ESP32 runs at 3.3 V logic.
For a 5 V output, use a divider, a level shifter, or pick a 3.3 V module.
textPreview: Logic level | The ESP32 runs at 3.3 V logic. | For a 5 V output, use a divider, a level shifter, or pick a 3.3 V module.

name: TextBox 7
text:
Current
A GPIO pin carries a signal, not power.
Never power motors, pumps, solenoids, bare relay coils or several servos straight from a pin.

text: Two supplies? Then tie the grounds together, unless they are properly isolated.

Duty cycle
The fraction of each period the pin spends HIGH.
0 % = off, 100 % = fully on.
Used for LED brightness, motor speed and heater power.

name: TextBox 5

The problem
A real signal wobbles around the threshold.
A single threshold makes the actuator switch on every wobble — noisy, and hard on a relay or servo.
Fix: switch on at one value and off at a lower one.
